articles.title: Real Estate Tech Startup MARC Raises $5M Seed Round
articles.narrative: MARC, an AI platform designed to help institutional real estate owners optimize operating costs, has successfully closed an oversubscribed $5 million seed funding round. This latest investment, led by Work-Bench with participation from MXV Capital and several prominent founders, brings the company's total funding to $6 million. The Manhattan-based startup plans to leverage the capital to accelerate its expansion across the U.S. and Canada, as well as grow its team in New York to meet increasing demand for its product.

articles.title: Get to Know the Broker: Joshua Young of Brown Harris Stevens
articles.narrative: This article profiles Joshua Young, Executive Vice President at Brown Harris Stevens and founder of the Young New Development Group, which specializes in marketing, leasing, and sales for new development projects. Young, who has over 20 years of experience in residential and commercial real estate, emphasizes the rewarding aspect of shaping a project from its inception, including unit mix, layouts, amenities, positioning, and pricing, rather than just focusing on sales numbers. He highlights the importance of collaboration with developers and the satisfaction of seeing these early decisions translate into market success.

data_points.address: 175 East 82nd Street, New York City, NY

articles.title: Manhattan Investment Sales Dip but Remain Ahead of 2025: Report
articles.narrative: Manhattan's investment sales volume experienced a 27% decline in Q3 2026, reaching $2.5 billion, marking the second consecutive quarterly drop. Despite this, the year-to-date sales volume of $9.61 billion is up 4% from 2025, and the market is on track for a record year in terms of total transactions. The market continues to see strong underlying fundamentals, particularly in multifamily and retail sectors, which are attracting capital despite headwinds like higher interest rates and geopolitical uncertainty. The buyer pool has shifted, with private buyers leading and REITs significantly increasing their share of dollar volume.

people.name: Brandon Polakoff
people.title: Principal and Head of New York City Investment Sales

articles.market_intelligence: Manhattan's investment sales market is experiencing a shift in buyer demographics, with private buyers taking the lead and REITs significantly increasing their market share from 7.3% in 2025 to 36% year-to-date in 2026. International and foreign buyers are pulling back. Multifamily and retail sectors show strong momentum, with multifamily dollar volume up 74% year-to-date and retail experiencing a 54% quarterly increase in dollar volume, driven by owner-user purchases. Development activity has slowed, with year-to-date dollar volume down 17% and average prices per square foot nearly halved from 2025 levels.

articles.title: Four Signals From the New York City Market That Matter More Than a Headline
articles.narrative: This opinion piece argues that the New York City residential real estate market is characterized by strategic, individual decisions rather than broad, uniform responses to market conditions. The author identifies four key patterns: sellers are increasingly opting to rent between selling and buying to maintain flexibility; investors are selectively acquiring properties with strong rental appeal, focusing on long-term value; desirable homes can still command above-asking prices when they meet specific buyer needs; and off-market transactions are becoming a more deliberate path, often facilitated by agent relationships and social media. The author concludes that understanding the market requires observing these intentional decisions rather than relying on single metrics or forecasts.

articles.title: Genting Lands $500M to Refi Mixed-Use Omni Center in Miami
articles.narrative: Genting Americas secured a $500 million refinancing loan for its 1.5 million-square-foot mixed-use Omni Center in Miami. The property, acquired by Genting in 2011 through foreclosure, includes office space, a Hilton hotel, and a large parking garage. This financing comes three years after Genting's unsuccessful attempt to sell an adjacent 15-acre site, which it had planned to develop into a casino.

data_points.notable_features: Features 435,000 square feet of office space, a 527-room Hilton hotel, and a 2,500-spot parking garage.
data_points.project_notes: Genting Americas purchased the asset for $180 million in 2011 through foreclosure. The adjacent 15-acre site was also acquired in 2011 for $236 million with plans for a casino that did not materialize.

articles.title: Broadview Real Estate Unveils Plans for 32-Story Office Tower in Houston
articles.narrative: Broadview Real Estate, a division of Broadview Capital, has announced plans for O27, a 32-story office tower in Houston's River Oaks area. The 520,000-square-foot development, designed by STG Design, will feature a distinctive geometric glass facade, street-level water features, and a landscaped terrace atop a nine-story parking deck. Completion of the project is anticipated in 2028.

data_points.notable_features: 32-story tower with a textured, geometric facade of triangular glass panels; includes street-level water features, a landscaped terrace, and a penthouse crown. The lobby features a suspended sculpture and ceiling lights evoking Houston's waterways and 'Space City' reputation.

articles.title: Partnership Acquires 358-Unit Apartment Community in Arlington
articles.narrative: A partnership between PCCP and RPM Living Investments has acquired Truman at Arlington Commons, a 358-unit apartment community in Arlington, TX. The four-story building, constructed in 2021, features a mix of studio to three-bedroom units and includes 4,900 square feet of retail space. The property offers a variety of amenities such as a pool, fitness center, and private event space.

articles.title: Jackson Walker Signs 110,000 SF Office Lease at The Republic in Downtown Austin
articles.narrative: Jackson Walker has signed a significant 110,000-square-foot office lease at The Republic, a newly constructed 48-story office tower in downtown Austin. The law firm will occupy three mid-level floors, marking a notable commitment to the city's central business district. The building is owned by a partnership of DivcoWest, Phoenix Property Group, and Lincoln Property Co., with Lincoln also managing the leasing.

articles.title: Finish Strong: Building Better Retailer-Contractor Partnerships
articles.narrative: This article, authored by Justin Elder of Elder-Jones, Inc. and the Retail Contractors Association, emphasizes the critical role of strong retailer-contractor partnerships in successful retail construction projects. The author argues that while construction variables are unavoidable, cost and schedule surprises can be mitigated through disciplined preconstruction, clear decision-making, and robust project controls. Key supporting points include the necessity of early contractor involvement for technical completeness, building schedules around retail operations, and establishing measurable communication protocols to ensure early visibility and efficient change management.

articles.title: Gaining strength: Milwaukee industrial market benefitting from strong demand for manufacturing space
articles.narrative: Milwaukee's industrial real estate market is experiencing a resurgence, primarily driven by robust demand for manufacturing facilities, according to a recent report. This increased demand has led to a significant improvement in occupancy rates and a notable decline in overall industrial vacancy, marking the first substantial drop since 2022. Despite challenges posed by trade policy uncertainty, a restrained development pipeline is expected to further support property performance and contribute to continued tightening of market conditions through the end of the year.
articles.market_intelligence: Manufacturing payrolls in the Milwaukee metro area edged higher during the first eight months of 2026 after declining steadily since 2023. The market recorded a decade-high level of manufacturing leasing, with occupancy gains across different property sizes. Older industrial buildings in established central Milwaukee County locations showed strong absorption. Warehouse market net absorption returned to 2022-2024 levels, supported by manufacturing-related storage and data-center development. Distribution properties, however, experienced negative net absorption for a third consecutive year. Approximately 1.65 million square feet of industrial space is forecast for completion in 2026, representing a 0.6% inventory increase, which is more than 40% below the prior 10-year average. Manufacturing space accounts for roughly 60% of projected completions. As of June, less than 1 million square feet was under construction, the lowest level since 2021. Nearly all submarkets recorded lower vacancy, with Ozaukee, Milwaukee, and Washington counties posting declines over 100 basis points. Waukesha County had the tightest industrial market at 2.4% vacancy. Average asking rents declined 2% in the first half of 2026 to $5.98 per square foot, with a full-year forecast of $6.16 per square foot. Industrial investment deal flow rose nearly 50%, with manufacturing property transactions reaching a multiyear high. Owner-users were net sellers for a sixth consecutive year, but acquisitions accelerated sharply in the first half of 2026, often involving pre-1990 properties. Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport plans a 333,000-square-foot South Air Cargo Facility, potentially quadrupling cargo capacity.

articles.title: Kraus-Anderson wraps construction on Waterfair Apartments in Wauwatosa
articles.narrative: Kraus-Anderson has completed the adaptive reuse and renovation of the former Sonesta Hotel in Wauwatosa, Wisconsin, transforming it into the Waterfair Apartments. This 146-unit multifamily project, designed by Continuum Architects + Planners, provides much-needed affordable housing in the Wauwatosa Research Park District, strategically located near major employment centers like the Milwaukee Regional Medical Center and the Milwaukee Regional Innovation Center. The development addresses a market need for below-market-rate housing in a job-dense area.

data_points.notable_features: Adaptive reuse of an eight-story hotel and convention space; features a first-floor amenity area with a community room, fitness center, media room, coffee lounge, conference/study rooms, and a large patio. Located near Wauwatosa Milwaukee Regional Medical Center (MRMC) and the Milwaukee Regional Innovation Center (MRIC).
data_points.project_notes: Converted a 198-unit hotel into 146 affordable apartments.

articles.title: Integrate Construction Partners wraps construction of fleet maintenance building for city of Clayton
articles.narrative: Integrate Construction Partners has completed the first phase of the City of Clayton's $11.7 million Municipal Maintenance Facility project, delivering a new 5,750-square-foot fleet maintenance building. This initial phase, which began in October 2025, involved constructing a facility designed to maintain the city's public works fleet, featuring multiple service bays, offices, and specialized equipment. The project team successfully managed significant logistical challenges, including working near a Metro Transit easement and coordinating deliveries under a low overpass, while also addressing environmental remediation for contaminated soils and groundwater. The second phase, expected to finish in January 2027, will involve extensive renovations to an existing 17,000-square-foot building and the construction of additional structures like a truck wash bay and storage canopies.

data_points.total_project_all_phases: Phase 2 includes renovation of 17,000-square-foot building, new 1,500-square-foot truck wash bay, 2,000-square-foot parking canopy, and 6,700-square-foot truck storage canopy, slated for completion January 2027.
data_points.notable_features: Building constructed with pre-engineered steel superstructure and conventional steel for mezzanine and material crane elements; includes offices, storage mezzanine, five-ton overhead crane maintenance bay, four vehicle service bays, and a tire and machine shop.
data_points.project_notes: Project launched in October 2025. Construction involved coordinating with city staff to minimize disruption to ongoing operations, navigating a Metro Transit easement, and managing deliveries under a low overpass. Remediation efforts were coordinated for contaminated soils and groundwater.

articles.title: Private-Label CMBS Accounts for Half of Delinquencies in Securitized Multifamily Loans
articles.narrative: A recent report by Trepp highlights that private-label CMBS now accounts for half of all delinquent securitized multifamily loans, despite representing only 12% of the total outstanding balance. This marks a significant shift from two years prior when CRE CLOs held the largest share of delinquent multifamily debt. The high delinquency rate in private-label CMBS, at 7.69%, contrasts sharply with Freddie Mac's 0.80% delinquency rate, suggesting a concentration of distress within the private-label segment. The report also notes that CRE CLO managers' ability to remove credit-impaired loans from pools might understate the true level of distress in that sector.

articles.title: AT&T Signs Five-Year Extension on Retail Space at 3 Times Square

This renewal underscores the continued appeal of Times Square as a high-traffic retail destination, following recent capital improvements to the building by the landlord.

articles.title: Barings Provides $139M Refi on Hillwood Industrial Campus
articles.narrative: Barings has provided $138.6 million in first mortgage financing to refinance the initial phase of Speedway Commerce Center, a two-building Class A industrial campus in Rancho Cucamonga, CA. The financing was extended to Hillwood, the developer of the fully leased, strategically located logistics asset. The property's modern features and excellent transportation connectivity contribute to its strong long-term demand in a key distribution market.

data_points.notable_features: Class A industrial buildings with high clear heights, ample trailer and automobile parking, and extensive loading capabilities. Immediate access to Interstate 10 and Interstate 15, providing connectivity throughout Southern California and access to the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach.

articles.title: Gilbane Development Acquires Sheepshead Bay Site Suited to Large-Scale Affordable Housing
articles.narrative: Gilbane Development has acquired a 96,000-square-foot development site at 2185 Coyle St. in Brooklyn's Sheepshead Bay for $37 million. The property, recently rezoned, offers 408,400 buildable square feet and is considered ideal for a large-scale affordable housing project. The transaction was facilitated by Ariel Property Advisors on behalf of the seller, a joint venture between AAG Management and ABS Partners.

data_points.notable_features: Recently rezoned property, ideally suited for large-scale affordable housing development.

articles.title: Debt Flood Shrinks Bank OZK's Real Estate Book Faster Than Planned
articles.narrative: Bank OZK, a prominent construction lender, has reduced its commercial real estate loan portfolio, a move influenced by market dynamics rather than solely strategic choice. This reduction indicates a shift in the bank's lending activity within the CRE sector.

articles.title: Development Constraints In Massachusetts Push More Investors To Southern New Hampshire
articles.narrative: Development constraints in Massachusetts, including the threat of rent control, high costs, and regulatory pressures, are prompting investors and developers to shift their focus to Southern New Hampshire. This migration is driven by a search for more favorable business environments and potentially higher returns.

articles.title: Manayunk Apartments Trade For $10M: The Philadelphia Deal Sheet
articles.narrative: The HOW Group has acquired the Yarn Factory Lofts, a multifamily property located in Manayunk, Philadelphia, for $10 million. This transaction highlights continued investment activity in the Philadelphia market.

articles.title: Developers Question Depth Of Miami's Branded Condo Craze
articles.narrative: Developers in Miami are currently evaluating the benefits and drawbacks of partnering with luxury brands such as Gucci, Bugatti, and Ritz-Carlton for branded condominium projects. This trend, while offering potential for premium pricing and market differentiation, also introduces complexities related to brand standards, design constraints, and increased development costs. The article explores the strategic considerations developers face in deciding whether to pursue these high-profile collaborations in the competitive Miami market.

articles.title: Conversions Ramp Up As New Report Calls For Resident-Led Downtown Denver Recovery
articles.narrative: A new report advocates for a resident-led recovery of downtown Denver, emphasizing the need for increased residential conversions. The city and various downtown advocacy groups have already invested millions to support these conversion projects, aiming to revitalize the urban core by boosting its residential population.
